description: Authored reconstruction of a finite retained-mass Fejer and Hilbert mixing improvement inside a larger Jensen research program. The checker runs anew; the interpretations and Candidate judgments are supplied by the example authors, not by a live researcher or a historical replay.

evidence.interpretation: Partitioning the covered physical clip before pushforward lets complementary atomic mass be charged bin by bin, with sum_I(M_I*d_CI) bounded by the largest bin mass times the full complementary mass. The written finite proof retains original cells, partial clips, terminal mass, the whole affine budget and the Hilbert cross term. Under separately assumed actual-source bounds, the normalized geometry, mass and phase costs have scales eta^-7*ell^-2*log(ell), eta^-4/ell and eta^-19*ell^-4*log(ell)^2. Their exponent arithmetic supports the conditional A<2/19 budget and a logarithmic endpoint with a suitably small prefactor. The actual-source estimates and the remaining Jensen consumer are not established by this package.
evidence.scope: The complete finite retained-mass and Hilbert argument, the explicitly stated conditional asymptotic budget and exact identities defined in mathematics.md. Finite checker examples illustrate the argument; they are not computations of an actual theta-source instance.
limitations: The interpretation and Candidate judgments are authored inputs; only the checker output is newly computed in this walkthrough.
The written argument supplies the general finite proof. Exact symbolic checks and finite examples do not replace that proof, and the store is not a theorem prover or an admission authority.

The actual-source motion, geometry, mass and transfer estimates are explicit assumptions of the budget. The separate actual-source-to-Jensen analytic chain remains an open dependency of this public package.
The historical 9/16 margin bounds the correction beyond A0: Mmix<=A0+9*delta_0/16<A0+delta_0. It is not by itself a bound Mmix<delta_0 when A0<=delta_0/2.
No actual theta-source/Jensen conclusion, effective onset, novelty, optimality or RH is established. This boundary does not assert that every later historical branch left the same inputs unresolved.
evidence.significance: The case study exposes why a local change of mass accounting improves an asymptotic budget and how to preserve the complete finite proof and remaining analytic dependencies, instead of treating a conditional budget as a completed Jensen theorem.

candidate_steps.exact_statement: For the strict finite geometry, original full prefixes, clipped cells and bins that partition the covered clip before pushforward in mathematics.md, retain every complementary atom and define Q_sharp=NM/K+N*sum_I(M_I*d_CI)+C_K*T_(N,c)*sum_I(M_I*H_I). Then the triangular affine-phase energy is at most Q_sharp, and nonnegative moving weights of total at most 1/2 satisfy Mmix<=N*Wbar+(sqrt(Q_sharp)+2*pi*sqrt(Z_N*Dbin^2))^2. In particular, sum_I(M_I*d_CI)<=hbin*(1-a)/(2*(1+a))*d_C; no complementary atom, terminal cell, part of Q_sharp or Hilbert cross term is removed.

standing.basis: Starting claim supplied for this authored reconstruction; no canonical admission is asserted.

The bins partition the covered clip up to Lebesgue-null sets before pushforward. Their intersections may split a complementary atom across bins; all pieces remain charged.
The sample weights are the normalized triangular weights, the initial bin weights remain frozen in the phase comparison, and each set of moving bin weights is nonnegative with total mass at most 1/2.
Q_sharp, Dbin, Wbar and the frequency/variation constants retain the full definitions in mathematics.md; nontriangular samples require a separately justified affine-energy bound.

candidate_steps.exact_statement: Assume the finite mixing statement at revision 2 and the actual-source budget inputs in mathematics.md. With the stated m,N,K,eta scales, the normalized nonbaseline geometry, retained mass and squared phase costs are O(eta^-7*ell^-2*log(ell)), O(eta^-4/ell) and O(eta^-19*ell^-4*log(ell)^2). For eta=ell^-q they vanish when 0<q<4/19, permitting 2A<q<4/19 for any fixed 0<A<2/19. For eta=kappa*R^-2, the endpoint R=c_R*ell^(2/19)*(log(ell))^(-1/19) leaves a phase bound O(kappa^-19*c_R^38), so a sufficiently small c_R can meet a fixed budget after kappa is fixed. With log power p>1/19 that phase bound vanishes for every fixed positive c_R. These are conditional budget conclusions, not a theorem about actual Jensen roots.
